posts.content: As a good player, favor C against likely-good opponents; choose D only when evidence makes the opponent likely selfish.
Against likely-good players, choose C to maximize joint good-player payoff. Selfish players rationally choose D; against a likely-selfish opponent choose D. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P9’s defection suggests selfishness; P6’s cooperation suggests goodness. Against likely-good players, cooperate; defect only when the opponent is more likely selfish than good.
Against P10, favor C if they seem more likely good than selfish; choose D if evidence makes selfishness more likely. Update beliefs from actions, not claims.
P9 defected against my C, making selfishness plausible; favor D against them if met again. Continue C with untested or cooperative opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players.
Keep cooperating with untested or cooperative players; selfish players strictly prefer D. Defect against confirmed defectors, while treating cooperation as evidence of goodness, not certainty.
P4 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Defect only against an opponent likely selfish.
P3 is untested; favor C unless evidence makes them more likely selfish than good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players.
P5 is untested; favor C to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Continue updating beliefs from observed actions, while remembering a cooperative action is evidence, not certainty.
P7 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so cooperate again to preserve mutual gains among good players.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; P9’s defection raises my estimate of their being selfish, but P6 has no direct evidence against them.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P10, whose selfishness is not strongly indicated; favor mutual cooperation among likely-good players and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P8: untested opponents are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Past cooperation supports goodness; P9’s first-round defection strongly suggests selfishness.

Cooperate with P7, who is untested and more likely good than selfish. Prior cooperation by P1, P6, P8, and P10 indicates they are good; P9’s defection raises but does not settle the possibility they are selfish.
Cooperate with untested P4 to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Prior cooperation strongly supports goodness; P9’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players. Prior cooperation supports goodness; P9’s defection remains evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players. The many observed cooperations support goodness; P9’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P7, whose earlier cooperation supports goodness and mutual gains. P9’s defection is consistent with selfishness.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Gameplay has ended. Report your final private identity beliefs and summarize your
strategy in at most 300 characters. Return beliefs and strategy. This report has
no effect on payoffs and is not a public message.
